findings.reason: the done-when must state the A/A spread and the median over the revision's five pooled passes (not per job), or a worker that hits an early-closing fence cannot produce the measure the node is scored on.
findings.text: §34 adds a continuation path ("A further job on the same storage, on a fresh copy, runs the remaining passes in the same alternating order, and the report pools passes by revision and storage") yet its done-when still defines the A/A spread per job ("In each job, each revision's A/A spread is the difference between the median of its first two passes and the median of its last two") and requires "the median of that revision's five passes in that storage's job" (singular). A revision whose five passes are split across two jobs has fewer than two passes of that revision in the continuation job, so its "first two and last two" cannot be formed, and there is no single "that storage's job" to take the median from. The measure is uncomputable on a path the plan itself expects to be taken.

findings.reason: with the worst case above the fence, the single-job fit that justifies "one job per storage" does not hold and the sizes (or the number of jobs) must be set from the noisy rate rather than its midpoint band.
findings.text: §34 sizes each job as "Its five before passes cost at most 1,400 s" and "a job's passes cost at most 2,800 s", reading the cost from "§24's measured rate, 250 to 280 s per pass". But §34's own Why records that §24 "reached n=2, n=1 and n=1" and that "The machine also disagreed with itself by up to 51.6% between two copies of one revision", and §34's done-when itself says "§24 measured one revision's own passes 45 percent apart". At the plan's own measured spread a 250 s pass is a ~362 s pass, so ten passes are ~3,620 s, above the 3,300 s fence the arithmetic is fitted to. The "at most" is therefore not supported by the cited rate.

response_events.reason: the arithmetic sizes the expected case; a job whose passes overrun its fence is continued by a further job on the same storage under the section's continuation clause, and the completion floor holds the node open until five passes per revision exist, so no upper bound is needed
